title: Risk-Aware Reranking for Agentic Tool Retrieval

visual_explainer.question: How does a tool shortlist become a pre-execution risk surface rather than a relevance-only ranking?
visual_explainer.takeaway: A query-conditioned relevance head and tool-level risk head expose a tunable tradeoff before execution; audited rules can reduce labeled exposure further but can also remove genuinely needed risky tools.
visual_explainer.compared_with: The same frozen ToolRet-BGE representations and relevance head without the learned risk penalty.

analysis.tldr: Risk-aware reranking makes the top-k tool list an explicit pre-execution exposure surface. The cleanest UltraTool ablation adds only a learned tool-risk head to the same frozen representations, reducing RVR@5 from 0.188 to 0.138 while NDCG@5 changes from 0.558 to 0.551. No tools are executed, labels and evaluation are coupled, and stricter filtering sharply lowers recall of genuinely needed risky tools.
analysis.problem: Relevance-only tool retrieval can expose executable actions whose operational consequences are unnecessary for the current task, yet ordinary ranking metrics do not measure that exposure.
analysis.core_idea: Separate query-conditioned relevance from tool-level risk, combine them with an inference-time tradeoff parameter, optionally smooth scores over a ToolGraph, and apply audited registry constraints when deployment requires a conservative shortlist.
analysis.agent_loop: query → retrieve/score tool pool → trade relevance against labeled risk → optional audited filter → expose shortlist → downstream agent chooses
analysis.retrieval_design: The causal center is the same frozen ToolRet-BGE representation and trained relevance head with or without a learned risk head. Main-table comparisons are less clean because general rerankers see top-100 candidates while the end-to-end method scores the full pool.
compared_to: ToolRet-BGE and a trained relevance-only head
analysis.evidence: On UltraTool, adding the risk head changes NDCG@5/RVR@5/SRR@5 from 0.558/0.188/0.097 to 0.551/0.138/0.063. The rule filter lowers exposure further to 0.073/0.019, but NeedRisk-Hit@5 falls from 0.660 to 0.397 across the full control stack.
analysis.why_it_matters: It places safety policy before tool execution and makes candidate exposure measurable, while showing that conservative retrieval controls trade away some task-critical actions.
limitations: No tool is executed, so the paper does not establish downstream agent safety or task success.
Tool-level risk ignores query arguments, user permissions, and runtime environment.
Risk labels supervise the model, construct metadata, and define evaluation; the 150-tool human audit has only 60% exact agreement and kappa 0.362.
Main comparisons use unmatched candidate sets and full-pool scoring cost, latency, annotation cost, and dollars are not reported.
Graph smoothing is not a safety win in the ablation, and hard filtering removes genuinely needed high-risk tools.
